Inventory and profile a database in one call

Source: R/run.R
inventory_run.Rd

The end-to-end run: connect, build the inventory (artefact 1), write it to the store, profile every column (artefact 2) with per-table checkpointing, optionally export CSV or Parquet and render the report. Re-running with the same store resumes an interrupted profile; pass resume = FALSE to start over.

Usage

inventory_run(
  source,
  store = "db_inventory.sqlite",
  export_dir = NULL,
  export_format = c("csv", "parquet"),
  report = NULL,
  schema = NULL,
  include = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  views = TRUE,
  sample_rows = 1e+06,
  top_n = 10,
  full_set_max = 50,
  top_values_max_distinct = 10000,
  keep_values = FALSE,
  resume = TRUE,
  sizes = TRUE,
  dialect = NULL,
  progress = interactive(),
  disconnect = TRUE
)

Arguments

source

Anything db_connect() accepts: a DBIConnection, an ODBC connection string or DSN, a SQLite or DuckDB file, or a Parquet file or directory.

store

Path to the SQLite results store. Default "db_inventory.sqlite" in the working directory.

export_dir

If given, the store is exported here after the run.

export_format

"csv" (default) or "parquet".

report

If given, the path of an HTML report to render, see render_report().

schema

Optional character vector of schema names to keep.

include, exclude

Optional regular expressions matched (case insensitively) against "schema.table". A table is kept if it matches any include pattern and no exclude pattern.

views

Keep views as well as base tables? Default TRUE.

sample_rows

Tables with more rows than this are profiled on a sample of roughly this many rows. Inf disables sampling.

top_n

How many most-frequent values to record per column.

full_set_max

Columns with at most this many distinct values have every value recorded, not just the top top_n, so that a code list's frequency table is complete and foreign key membership can be tested against it.

top_values_max_distinct

Only compute top values for columns with at most this many distinct values; beyond that a frequency table says little.

keep_values

If FALSE (the default) the literal min, max and top values of columns inferred as identifiers or free text, or whose names suggest personal data, are suppressed and only their hashes kept. Set TRUE on a system where the profile output is itself safe to hold.

resume

Skip tables already profiled in store? Default TRUE.

sizes

Read table sizes from system views? Default TRUE.

dialect

Optional dialect override, see db_dialect().

progress

Show progress bars? Default TRUE in interactive use.

disconnect

Disconnect a connection this function opened? Default TRUE; a connection passed in is never closed.

Value

Invisibly, a list with inventory (a db_inventory), profile (a column_profile, the full contents of the store including earlier runs) and store (the store path).

Examples

out <- inventory_run(fakehosp_path(), store = tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"),
                     include = "pas_patients", progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ 1 table found (sqlite dialect)
#> ✔ Inventory of 1 table and 10 columns in 0s
#> ℹ 0 foreign key candidates proposed
#> ✔ Run complete in 0.1s: 10 column profiles in /tmp/RtmpDjk1SO/file1ac85ce3ab74.sqlite
out$profile[, c("column_name", "semantic_type", "null_rate")]
#> # A tibble: 10 × 3
#>    column_name         semantic_type null_rate
#>    <chr>               <chr>             <dbl>
#>  1 mrn                 identifier        0    
#>  2 nhs_number          identifier        0.007
#>  3 nhs_number_status   code              0    
#>  4 sex                 code              0    
#>  5 dob                 date              0    
#>  6 ethnicity           code              0    
#>  7 gp_practice         category          0    
#>  8 postcode            identifier        0    
#>  9 registered_datetime datetime          0    
#> 10 date_of_death       date              0.987
